label: first occurrence of w/a/g/n/b/j/v at original positions 2-6
explanation: Fires only in the original input phase (100% of mass), never at t=0, the delimiter, or during copying. It peaks at positions 2-5 (t=3 is highest) and fades by t=7. It strongly prefers letters input for the first time, mainly w and a (4.5x lift), then g, n, b (about 3x) and more weakly j, v, o, e. Repeated tokens rarely fire it (in_first=0 carries 7% of mass). Magnitude depends on the prefix: the largest activations come in sequences that start with 1, 3, h or d (e.g. 1 h j 3 [w]). The same token after other prefixes is often inactive, which is why precision is only around 0.45. The predicate gives dev F1 0.49 and mass recall 0.65; adding prefix-set conditions did not help. This looks like a distributed code over current token, position and prefix content rather than a single clean concept.
